title: Consolidate post-merge via BranchMerger.consolidate primitive and ChangesetDigest prompt input
summary: Close all four facets of the consolidation bug class (#5 Bug A, Bug B, Mode 3; #12; #13) by replacing `BranchMerger.merge_and_push` with one total-function primitive `consolidate(...) -> ConsolidationOutcome` whose four mutually exclusive statuses (`ALREADY_INTEGRATED`, `FAST_FORWARDED`, `DIVERGENT`, `SOURCE_MISSING`) callers route on (no `try/except`, no silent skip, no `phase` discriminant); making the evaluator prompt accept a typed `ChangesetDigest` data object pre-computed by the engine via a new `GitService.diff_summary` (no shell-command strings in the prompt body); renaming `WorkflowState.last_commit_sha` → `feature_tip_sha`; preserving the per-iter `WorkflowIterationEvent.commit_sha` semantic via a new `RalphLoopState.iteration_commit_sha: NotRequired[str | None]` (PEP 655); typing the persister's success path with `PersistResult.source: PersistSource` (no `<agent-direct>` sentinel string); and DELETING `GitWorktreeProvider._backup_if_needed` so the silent backup-branch creator that produces issue #13's `-backup-<hex>` topology is gone. Every reviewer concern from the previous draft is addressed: no boolean discriminants, no exception-swallowing, no string-literal cross-component contracts, no YAGNI fields, no parallel ff-bypass methods, no `git status --porcelain` reliance for commit detection.
context:
A previous draft was rejected. The reviewer agreed with the diagnosis (all four issues share one architectural root: silent-skip + assumed-universal-ff in the consolidation path) but flagged that the proposed remedy re-introduced the very anti-patterns it was meant to eliminate. This revision was produced after re-investigating the codebase (every reviewer claim verified against actual files via Explore agents) and re-consulting the relevant first-party documentation.

Verified facts from re-investigation:
- `GitWorktreeProvider._backup_if_needed` (src/kodezart/adapters/git_worktree_provider.py:102-142) is the actual creator of issue #13's `-backup-<hex>` branches. It is called on every `release()` (line 98), commits uncommitted work with "kodezart: emergency backup of in-progress work" (line 121), and pushes to a `BackupBranchName`-derived branch (line 131). The previous draft punted on this as out-of-scope; reviewer required it be brought into the typed contract or disabled.
- `tests/prompts/test_prompt_wiring.py` already exists (41 lines) and tests `evaluation.build_prompt` positionally at line 15 — a new `tests/prompts/test_evaluation.py` would be duplicate (DRY violation per reviewer). Extend the existing file.
- `tests/chains/test_ralph_loop.py:413-431` contains a positional `build_prompt` spy used by `test_loop_re_evaluates_all_criteria_every_iteration` — the spy signature must migrate alongside the production signature change.
- `tests/chains/test_ralph_workflow.py:205-232` (`test_workflow_merge_failure_reports_error`) injects `FakeBranchMerger(fail=RuntimeError("merge conflict"))`. Under the new `consolidate` contract that never raises on DIVERGENT, the test must be reshaped to inject a DIVERGENT outcome while preserving the same `WorkflowCompleteEvent.error` assertion surface.
- `tests/chains/test_ralph_workflow.py:194-202`, `tests/chains/test_shorthand_url_resolution.py:87-89`, `tests/chains/test_ralph_workflow.py:2026-2028` all assert `len(merger.calls) == 3` (merge_and_push + cleanup_source + cleanup_backup_branches). After consolidation absorbs cleanup_source internally, the count becomes 2 (consolidate + cleanup_backup_branches).
- `src/kodezart/main.py:54-113` instantiates `git = SubprocessGitService(auth=auth)` (line 54) and `cache` (line 56) in scope; both are trivially passable to new `RalphWorkflowEngine(..., git=git, cache=cache)` and `RalphLoop(..., git=git, cache=cache)` constructor parameters.
- `NotRequired` (PEP 655) is in `typing` since Python 3.11; project targets 3.12.
- `enum.StrEnum` added in 3.11; recommended over `class Foo(str, Enum)` for 3.11+.
- `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads <remote> refs/heads/<branch>` exits 2 when no matching refs found (per git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-remote.html); without `--exit-code` the command exits 0 silently — adapter MUST use `--exit-code` and map exit 2 → None explicitly.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 0 iff ancestor, 1 iff not (per git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-base); anything else is an error — adapter uses a new `_run_with_exit_codes(allowed={0, 1})` helper.
- `git ls-remote` queries the remote directly — NO `git fetch` is needed before. `git fetch` IS needed before in-worktree `is_ancestor` calls (operates on local refs).
- Pydantic v2 discriminated-union backward compat is NOT automatic (docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/unions/): SSE consumers parsing against a closed union with `extra="forbid"` will reject `workflow_consolidation` unless their schema is updated. A snapshot test of the camelCase wire shape is added as the explicit coordination artifact.
- `_run` in subprocess_git_service.py:216-235 raises on non-zero exit; new helper required for ls-remote (exit 2 valid) and merge-base --is-ancestor (exit 1 valid).
- PersistResult is `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` with `commit_sha`, `branch`, `message` — extending with required `source: PersistSource` is fully additive at the only consumer (`agent_service.py:167-179` reads only commit_sha and branch).
- All AgentEvent subclasses pass through one uniform `model_dump(by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)` call in `agent_handler.py:52,78` — new event types need no handler-side wiring.

First-party documentation consulted:
- LangGraph state management — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-graph-api (TypedDict default-overwrite reducer; nodes omit unwritten keys).
- PEP 655 — https://peps.python.org/pep-0655/ (NotRequired semantics; available in `typing` from Python 3.11).
- Python enum.StrEnum — https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html (Python 3.11+; serializes naturally with Pydantic v2).
- git merge-base — https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-base (`--is-ancestor` exit codes).
- git ls-remote — https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-remote.html (`--exit-code` flag; no fetch required).
- git diff — https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff (`--name-only base..head`).
- Pydantic v2 discriminated unions — https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/unions/ (adding Literal variants is NOT automatically backwards-compatible for closed-union consumers).

references.note: `_execute_node` currently returns `{'iteration': ..., 'last_commit_sha': commit_sha}` unconditionally (root of #5 Bug A). After fix: always returns `{'iteration': ..., 'iteration_commit_sha': commit_sha}` — `iteration_commit_sha` is NotRequired[str | None] per PEP 655 and carries the per-iter semantic (None on no-change iter). NO cumulative `last_commit_sha`.

`_evaluate_node` currently emits `WorkflowIterationEvent(commit_sha=state['last_commit_sha'])` — clobbered to None on no-change iters. After fix: emits `commit_sha=state.get('iteration_commit_sha')` (per-iter semantic preserved) AND pre-computes `changeset = await self._git.diff_summary(cwd, base_ref=ctx.base_branch, head_ref=ctx.ralph_branch)` and passes `changeset` to `evaluation.build_prompt` (closes #12 inside the loop). Reviewer concern Q is addressed: the event field doesn't silently shift to 'latest known'.
`initial_state` in RalphLoop.run() — drop `last_commit_sha`; do NOT seed `iteration_commit_sha` (it's NotRequired, written by _execute_node every iter).

`_run_ralph_loop_node` — return `{'accepted': ..., 'total_iterations': ..., 'feature_tip_sha': None}`. Do NOT query the canonical ralph tip here; `consolidate` queries it internally via `remote_branch_sha`. The outer engine does the bookkeeping (reviewer concern, sanity-1).

`_merge_to_feature_node` — drop the `state['accepted'] and state['last_commit_sha'] is not None` guard AND the `try/except Exception` around `merge_and_push`. Replace with: if not accepted return early; else `outcome = await self._merger.consolidate(...)` and route on `outcome.status`. Emit `WorkflowConsolidationEvent` regardless. SOURCE_MISSING raises (programming error). DIVERGENT returns `merged=False, merge_error=...` (routes to `complete` via existing `_route_after_merge`). FAST_FORWARDED/ALREADY_INTEGRATED resolve `review_base_sha=remote_branch_sha(origin, base_branch)` and `review_head_sha=outcome.feature_tip_sha`.

`_route_after_merge` — unchanged in shape: routes to `review_against_ticket` on `merged`, `complete` otherwise. DIVERGENT now flows through with `merge_error` populated in state for `WorkflowCompleteEvent.error`.

`_review_against_ticket_node` — currently calls `evaluation_prompt.build_prompt(state['acceptance_criteria'])` (positional, no changeset — root of #12). After fix: assert `state['review_base_sha']` and `state['review_head_sha']` are not None, compute `changeset = await self._git.diff_summary(cwd, base_ref=state['review_base_sha'], head_ref=state['review_head_sha'])`, call `evaluation_prompt.build_prompt(criteria=state['acceptance_criteria'], changeset=changeset)`.

`_fix_code_node` — currently calls `merger.merge_and_push(base_branch=ctx.base_branch, source_branch=fix_branch)` (root of #5 Mode 3 — worktree acquired on `ctx.base_branch`='main' while `fix_branch` is descended from `feature_branch`). After fix: `outcome = await self._merger.consolidate(base_branch=state['feature_branch'], feature_branch=state['feature_branch'], source_branch=fix_branch, ...)`; emit `WorkflowConsolidationEvent` (no phase field). DIVERGENT/SOURCE_MISSING populate `merge_error` and route via the new conditional edge. ALREADY_INTEGRATED is legal (no exception). NO try/except.

Currently `graph.add_edge('fix_code', 'review_against_ticket')` (unconditional). Change to `graph.add_conditional_edges('fix_code', self._route_after_fix, {'review_against_ticket': ..., 'comment_failure': ..., 'complete': ...})`. New router `_route_after_fix` returns `review_against_ticket` when `merge_error is None`, `comment_failure` when `pr_url` set AND `_pr_creator is not None`, else `complete`. Reviewer concern P.

`_complete_node` — `final_commit_sha=state['feature_tip_sha']` (renamed source field; wire-format field name `final_commit_sha` / `finalCommitSha` is unchanged so existing consumers continue to read it).

`persist` short-circuits on `has_changes` only (root of #5 Bug B). After fix: clean-tree path queries `remote_branch_sha` + `current_sha`; if equal → None; if HEAD descends from remote tip → push + return `PersistResult(source=AGENT_DIRECT_COMMIT, message=<real HEAD message from git log -1 --format=%B HEAD>)`; else raise `RuntimeError` describing divergence.

`_backup_if_needed` — DELETE this method entirely. Its caller at line 98 (`release()`) replaces the call with `_log_release_state(workspace_path, info)` which only logs `workspace_release_unclean` on dirty release; does NOT push to any backup branch. Closes #13 at the source.

`_run` raises on any non-zero exit. New sibling `_run_with_exit_codes(cmd, cwd, allowed: frozenset[int], env=None) -> tuple[int, str]` tolerates declared exit codes (1 for is-ancestor, 2 for ls-remote --exit-code) and returns (exit_code, stdout); raises on anything else. The existing `_run` and `_run_output` are unchanged.

`merge_and_push` and public `cleanup_source` are REMOVED. `consolidate` is implemented with the four-status decision tree. Private `_cleanup_source_internal` (body of the old public `cleanup_source`) is invoked only on FAST_FORWARDED. `cleanup_backup_branches` is unchanged.
`GitService` — add `is_ancestor`, `remote_branch_sha`, `diff_summary`. NO `rev_list_count`, NO `diff_name_only` (YAGNI per reviewer concerns sanity-2, sanity-3).

`BranchMerger` — remove `merge_and_push` and `cleanup_source`; add `consolidate(...) -> ConsolidationOutcome`; keep `cleanup_backup_branches`. `consolidate` never raises on DIVERGENT/SOURCE_MISSING — total function over the four statuses.
Only call site of `_persister.persist(...)`. Reads `persist_result.commit_sha` and `persist_result.branch` — additive `PersistResult.source` field is consumer-transparent.

`WorkflowIterationEvent.commit_sha` field — semantic preserved as 'this iter's commit' by sourcing from `RalphLoopState.iteration_commit_sha` (NotRequired, per-iter) rather than from a cumulative state field. NO `ralph_tip_sha` field is added.

`PersistResult` — add required `source: PersistSource` field (no default). Add `PersistSource(StrEnum)` with members `WORKING_TREE_COMMIT`, `AGENT_DIRECT_COMMIT`. NO `<agent-direct>` sentinel string anywhere.
`RalphLoopState` — drop `last_commit_sha`; add `iteration_commit_sha: NotRequired[str | None]` from `typing`.
`WorkflowState` — rename `last_commit_sha` → `feature_tip_sha`; add `review_base_sha: str | None`, `review_head_sha: str | None`. NO `last_consolidation`, NO `ralph_tip_sha`.

`build_prompt` — keyword-only `(*, criteria, changeset)`. Inlines `ChangesetDigest` data verbatim (file paths, commit subjects, count). Empty-changeset case rendered as explicit escape clause. NO shell command strings in the prompt body.

Positional caller of `evaluation_prompt(['Tests pass'])` — migrate to keyword-only call with a `ChangesetDigest`. Extend this file with the three new tests; do NOT create `test_evaluation.py` (DRY per reviewer concern T).
Positional `build_prompt` spy — migrate signature to `def spy(*, criteria, changeset)`. Add per-iter regression tests covering `iteration_commit_sha`.
`assert len(merger.calls) == 3` → `assert len(merger.calls) == 2` (consolidate + cleanup_backup_branches). Update kwargs access on `merger.calls[0]`.

`test_workflow_merge_failure_reports_error` — reshape from `FakeBranchMerger(fail=RuntimeError(...))` to `FakeBranchMerger(consolidation_outcomes=[ConsolidationOutcome(status=DIVERGENT, feature_tip_sha='0'*40)])`. Same assertion surface preserved: `'diverged' in complete_events[0].error`.
P2-AC14: keep comment; update filter to `[c for c in merger.calls if c.get('method') == 'consolidate']`; assert count == 3 (1 initial + 2 fixes).
Same migration pattern as test_ralph_workflow.py:194-202; count 3 → 2; read `merger.calls[0]['repo_url']` on consolidate call.
Rename `test_merge_and_push_creates_feature_branch` → `test_consolidate_fast_forwarded_creates_feature_branch`. Add the three sibling status tests.
`FakeBranchMerger()` default-construct — verify new default outcome queue produces FAST_FORWARDED so existing API-layer `merged=True` assertions still pass.
Grep for `merge_and_push`, `cleanup_source`, `last_commit_sha`, `fail=`, positional `build_prompt`; migrate each in lockstep.

Existing backup-on-dirty-release test must be inverted: assert `workspace_release_unclean` warning AND assert `git.push` is NOT called with any backup-branch name. Add `test_backup_if_needed_method_is_gone` (introspection guard).
Composition root — add `git=git, cache=cache` kwargs to both `RalphLoop(...)` (line 85) and `RalphWorkflowEngine(...)` (line 100) constructor calls. Both already in scope.
LangGraph TypedDict default-overwrite reducer; nodes omit unwritten keys to skip update.
`NotRequired[T]` semantics — key may be absent at runtime; in `typing` since Python 3.11 (project targets 3.12).
`StrEnum` is Python 3.11+ idiomatic replacement for `class Foo(str, Enum)`; serializes naturally with Pydantic v2.
`--is-ancestor` exits 0 iff ancestor (ff possible), 1 iff not, else error.
`--exit-code` flag exits 2 when no matching refs; without it, exits 0 silently. Adapter MUST use `--exit-code`. NO `git fetch` required — ls-remote queries the remote directly.
`--name-only base..head` lists changed files; combined with `git log --no-merges --format=%s base..head` for `ChangesetDigest`.

Adding a new `Literal['workflow_consolidation']` variant to `AgentEvent` is NOT automatically backwards-compatible for SSE consumers parsing against a closed Pydantic-like discriminated union with `extra='forbid'`. Snapshot test of the camelCase wire shape is the explicit coordination artifact.

requiredChanges.description: New module. Defines `ConsolidationStatus(StrEnum)` with members ALREADY_INTEGRATED, FAST_FORWARDED, DIVERGENT, SOURCE_MISSING. Defines `ConsolidationOutcome(CamelCaseModel)` frozen with only `status: ConsolidationStatus` and `feature_tip_sha: str` (40-char Field). Defines `ChangesetDigest(CamelCaseModel)` frozen with `file_paths: list[str]`, `commit_subjects: list[str]`, `commit_count: int (>=0)`, and an `is_empty` property. Uses `model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)` which Pydantic v2 merges with the parent `CamelCaseModel` config (alias_generator=to_camel, populate_by_name=True, extra=forbid). Same inheritance pattern as `WorkflowContext` at `types/domain/workflow.py:30`.
requiredChanges.rationale: Single new types module for the consolidation primitive. `StrEnum` is the Python 3.11+ idiomatic replacement for `class Foo(str, Enum)` (reviewer concern L). Four-status partition eliminates the SOURCE_MISSING-vs-DIVERGENT overload the reviewer flagged (concern C). Only two fields on `ConsolidationOutcome` — `ahead_count`/`behind_count`/`source_tip_sha` are dropped as YAGNI per reviewer concern D. `ChangesetDigest` is the typed data object the engine pre-computes and the prompt inlines (reviewer concern B: no shell strings in prompt body).

requiredChanges.description: Add `PersistSource(StrEnum)` with `WORKING_TREE_COMMIT = 'working_tree_commit'` and `AGENT_DIRECT_COMMIT = 'agent_direct_commit'`. Extend `PersistResult` (the existing `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`) with a required `source: PersistSource` field (no default — every construction must specify the source).
requiredChanges.rationale: Replaces the `<agent-direct>` sentinel commit-message string (reviewer concern E: string-literal cross-component contracts are forbidden). The typed `source` field distinguishes the two persister paths externally without overloading the human-readable `message` field. The only existing consumer (agent_service.py:167-179) reads only `commit_sha` and `branch`, so the field is additive at the consumer side; only the persister's construction sites must pass `source=`.

requiredChanges.description: Add `WorkflowConsolidationEvent(AgentEvent)` with `type: Literal['workflow_consolidation']`, `status: ConsolidationStatus`, `feature_branch: str (min_length=1)`, `source_branch: str (min_length=1)`, `feature_tip_sha: str (min_length=40, max_length=40)`. NO `phase` field. NO change to `WorkflowIterationEvent`/`WorkflowReviewEvent`/`WorkflowPREvent`/`WorkflowCIEvent`/`WorkflowCompleteEvent` shapes. Import `ConsolidationStatus` from `kodezart.types.domain.consolidation`.
requiredChanges.rationale: Drops the `phase: Literal['post_loop', 'post_fix']` field — it was a renamed `fix_rounds_used == 0` vs `> 0` boolean discriminant (reviewer concern A: forbidden anti-pattern). Both emission sites differ by event ordering relative to `WorkflowReviewEvent` (existing convention). `WorkflowIterationEvent.commit_sha` keeps its per-iter semantic — no rename — because the per-iter value is sourced from the new `RalphLoopState.iteration_commit_sha` rather than from a cumulative state field (reviewer concern Q).

requiredChanges.description: `RalphLoopState`: REMOVE `last_commit_sha`. ADD `iteration_commit_sha: NotRequired[str | None]` (PEP 655 — `from typing import NotRequired`). `WorkflowState`: RENAME `last_commit_sha` → `feature_tip_sha: str | None`. ADD `review_base_sha: str | None` and `review_head_sha: str | None`. No `last_consolidation`. No `ralph_tip_sha`. No `ahead_count`/`behind_count`/`source_tip_sha`.
requiredChanges.rationale: `iteration_commit_sha: NotRequired[...]` preserves the per-iter `WorkflowIterationEvent.commit_sha` semantic without forcing a wire-shape rename (reviewer concern Q). The outer engine does NOT maintain a cumulative SHA — it queries `remote_branch_sha` once via `consolidate` (reviewer concern H). `feature_tip_sha` REPLACES `last_commit_sha` (not coexists — reviewer concern G). `review_base_sha`/`review_head_sha` are both 40-char SHAs only (not branch names) so the prompt receives canonical, unambiguous refs (reviewer concern F: no SHA-or-branch-name overload). `last_consolidation` field is dropped — only `status` was routed on, and the YAGNI fields would invite desync (reviewer concern D).

requiredChanges.description: On `GitService`: add three read-only async methods — `is_ancestor(cwd, ancestor_ref, descendant_ref) -> bool`, `remote_branch_sha(cwd, remote, branch) -> str | None` (NEVER raises on absent ref — returns None), `diff_summary(cwd, base_ref, head_ref) -> ChangesetDigest`. Do NOT add `rev_list_count` or `diff_name_only`. On `BranchMerger`: REMOVE `merge_and_push` and `cleanup_source`. ADD `consolidate(*, repo_path, repo_url, base_branch, feature_branch, source_branch, cache_key=None) -> ConsolidationOutcome` (NEVER raises on DIVERGENT/SOURCE_MISSING — total function). KEEP `cleanup_backup_branches`.
requiredChanges.rationale: `rev_list_count` is dropped — two `is_ancestor` calls partition all four statuses (reviewer concern, sanity-2). `diff_name_only` is dropped in favor of the higher-level `diff_summary` (reviewer concern, sanity-3). `cleanup_source` is removed from the protocol — it becomes a private adapter detail invoked only on FAST_FORWARDED, so the merger's decision tree no longer leaks into consumer nodes (reviewer concern, architecture-3: callers must NOT `match outcome.status` to decide whether to call cleanup_source). `consolidate` is single-responsibility (classify-and-merge); it's a total function over the four statuses.

requiredChanges.description: Add a private helper `_run_with_exit_codes(cmd, cwd, allowed: frozenset[int], env=None) -> tuple[int, str]` — runs the command, raises RuntimeError if exit not in `allowed`, returns `(exit_code, stdout)` otherwise. Implement: `is_ancestor` via `git merge-base --is-ancestor <a> <b>` with `allowed={0, 1}` (returns `exit_code == 0`); `remote_branch_sha` via `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads <remote> refs/heads/<branch>` with `allowed={0, 2}` (exit 2 → None; exit 0 → parse `<sha>\t<ref>` line and return SHA; NO `git fetch` before); `diff_summary` via parallel calls to `git diff --name-only <base>..<head>` and `git log --no-merges --format=%s <base>..<head>`, returns `ChangesetDigest(file_paths=..., commit_subjects=..., commit_count=len(subjects))`. Document the exit-code map in each method's docstring (especially `--exit-code` for ls-remote: 0=found, 2=no-match, else raise).
requiredChanges.rationale: Pure subprocess wrappers; no business logic. The new helper preserves the loud-failure invariant for unexpected exits (reviewer concern J: explicit empty-output → None mapping via `--exit-code`). NO `git fetch` before `remote_branch_sha` — official ls-remote docs confirm it queries the remote directly (reviewer concern I).

requiredChanges.description: REMOVE `merge_and_push` and `cleanup_source` (public). ADD private `_cleanup_source_internal` (body of old `cleanup_source`, never raises). Implement `consolidate` with this decision tree: (1) resolve bare-repo cwd; (2) query `source_tip = remote_branch_sha(cwd, origin, source_branch)` BEFORE acquiring a worktree — if None, resolve `feature_tip = remote_branch_sha(origin, feature_branch) or remote_branch_sha(origin, base_branch)` (raise if base_branch also missing on origin), return `SOURCE_MISSING`; (3) acquire worktree on `feature_branch` (creating from `base_branch` if absent); (4) `git fetch` (needed for in-worktree `is_ancestor` against local origin/* refs); (5) if `is_ancestor(workspace, source_tip, HEAD)` → ALREADY_INTEGRATED; (6) if `is_ancestor(workspace, HEAD, source_tip)` → `merge_branch(origin/<source_branch>)`, push, `_cleanup_source_internal`, return FAST_FORWARDED; (7) else DIVERGENT. NEVER raises on DIVERGENT/SOURCE_MISSING.
requiredChanges.rationale: Single source of truth for the consolidation decision tree (DRY). The SOURCE_MISSING path avoids acquiring a worktree to save round-trips (reviewer concern J + verified ls-remote behavior). `cleanup_source` is invoked internally only on FAST_FORWARDED — callers never need to know about it (reviewer concern, architecture-3). `git fetch` is needed here (before `is_ancestor`) but NOT before `remote_branch_sha` (reviewer concern I).

requiredChanges.description: Keep existing `has_changes` path; add a clean-tree branch. New flow: if `has_changes(workspace)` → existing path, return `PersistResult(..., source=PersistSource.WORKING_TREE_COMMIT)`. Else query `head_sha = current_sha(workspace)` and `remote_tip = remote_branch_sha(workspace, origin, branch)`; if equal → log `persist_no_changes`, return None; if `remote_tip is None or is_ancestor(workspace, remote_tip, head_sha)` → push, fetch real HEAD message via `git log -1 --format=%B HEAD`, return `PersistResult(commit_sha=head_sha, branch=branch, message=<head message>, source=PersistSource.AGENT_DIRECT_COMMIT)`; else raise `RuntimeError` describing the HEAD-vs-remote divergence. Expand the method docstring to describe the new conceptual scope ('ensure canonical ref equals workspace HEAD'). NO `<agent-direct>` sentinel.
requiredChanges.rationale: Closes #5 Bug B without relaxing `has_changes` semantics. The agent-direct path uses committed-history primitives only (no `git status --porcelain` reliance — anti-pattern honored). Divergence raises loudly. The real HEAD commit message is fetched via git — no sentinel strings (reviewer concern E + U). Reviewer accepted the option of keeping ONE `persist` method with documented expanded scope rather than splitting into `persist_changes` + `rescue_unpushed_commits`.

requiredChanges.description: DELETE the `_backup_if_needed` method (current lines 102-142). REMOVE its call from `release()` (line 98). ADD `_log_release_state(workspace_path, info)` which calls `has_changes` and emits `await self._log.awarning('workspace_release_unclean', ...)` when dirty, but does NOT push to any backup branch. Update the class docstring to document explicitly: 'Recovery-via-backup-branch is intentionally disabled; re-introducing it must be via the typed state contract — see the consolidation plan\'s out-of-scope note.'
requiredChanges.rationale: Closes #13 at the source — the silent backup-branch creator is gone (reviewer concern R + brief anti-pattern: 'No new -backup-<hex> branch lifecycle introduced without a corresponding WorkflowState field and SSE event'). The new persister contract ensures the canonical ref equals HEAD before release, so dirty state at release is a programming error elsewhere. Loud-via-warning surfaces the bug rather than masking it with a silent backup push. The class docstring records the deliberate trade-off so any future re-introduction is gated through a typed contract design.

requiredChanges.description: Change `build_prompt` signature to `(*, criteria: list[str], changeset: ChangesetDigest) -> str` (keyword-only). Inline a `── CHANGESET TO EVALUATE ──` block that renders `changeset.file_paths` as a numbered list and `changeset.commit_subjects` as a numbered list, plus `changeset.commit_count`. When `changeset.is_empty` is True, render an explicit empty-changeset note ('No commits between the base and head refs; the previous verdict\'s failures persist unchanged.') as the entire block. NO shell command strings in the prompt body. Keep the `_EVALUATION_PRELUDE` Watson sections otherwise unchanged.
requiredChanges.rationale: Closes #12. The prompt receives DATA (typed `ChangesetDigest`), not shell commands the agent must execute (reviewer concern B: 'data not commands'). Keyword-only enforces the contract at type-check time. The empty-changeset case is rendered explicitly so the reviewer cannot silently 'Cannot verify'.

requiredChanges.description: Add `git: GitService` and `cache: RepoCache` parameters to `__init__` (documented as single-purpose: `_evaluate_node` pre-computes `ChangesetDigest` for the evaluator prompt; the loop does NOT do canonical-tip bookkeeping). In `_execute_node`, always return `{'iteration': iteration, 'iteration_commit_sha': commit_sha}` — `commit_sha` is None on no-change iters. NO `last_commit_sha`. NO `ralph_tip_sha` resolution. In `_evaluate_node`, resolve `cwd = ctx.repo_path or await self._cache.ensure_available(ctx.repo_url, ctx.cache_key)`, call `changeset = await self._git.diff_summary(cwd=cwd, base_ref=ctx.base_branch, head_ref=ctx.ralph_branch)`, call `evaluation.build_prompt(criteria=ctx.acceptance_criteria, changeset=changeset)`, emit `WorkflowIterationEvent(commit_sha=state.get('iteration_commit_sha'), ...)` (per-iter semantic — may be None). In `run()`, the initial state drops `last_commit_sha` entirely (`iteration_commit_sha` is NotRequired and not seeded).
requiredChanges.rationale: Closes #5 Bug A — `iteration_commit_sha` is always written by `_execute_node` with the correct per-iter semantic (None when no commit, SHA otherwise); `_evaluate_node` reads it for the event field. The per-iter `WorkflowIterationEvent.commit_sha` does NOT silently shift to 'latest known' (reviewer concern Q). The loop does NOT take on canonical-tip bookkeeping — the outer engine does that via `consolidate`'s internal `remote_branch_sha` query (reviewer concern, sanity-1). `GitService`/`RepoCache` injection is the minimal widening needed solely for `diff_summary` in `_evaluate_node` (no shell commands in the loop's evaluator prompt either).

requiredChanges.description: Add `git: GitService` and `cache: RepoCache` parameters to `__init__`. Update `run()`'s `initial_state` to use `feature_tip_sha`, `review_base_sha`, `review_head_sha` (all None) — no `last_commit_sha`. In `_run_ralph_loop_node`, return `{'accepted': ..., 'total_iterations': ..., 'feature_tip_sha': None}` — do NOT query the canonical ralph tip here (the merger does that internally). In `_merge_to_feature_node`, drop the `try/except` around the merger call; call `outcome = await self._merger.consolidate(...)`; emit `WorkflowConsolidationEvent(status=outcome.status, feature_branch=..., source_branch=state['ralph_branch'], feature_tip_sha=outcome.feature_tip_sha)`; map status: SOURCE_MISSING → raise RuntimeError (programming error: loop ran but never pushed); DIVERGENT → `{'merged': False, 'merge_error': 'ralph diverged from feature: ...', 'feature_tip_sha': outcome.feature_tip_sha}`; FAST_FORWARDED or ALREADY_INTEGRATED → resolve `base_tip = await self._git.remote_branch_sha(cwd, 'origin', ctx.base_branch)` (raise if None), return `{'merged': True, 'merge_error': None, 'feature_tip_sha': outcome.feature_tip_sha, 'review_base_sha': base_tip, 'review_head_sha': outcome.feature_tip_sha}`. In `_review_against_ticket_node`, raise if `review_base_sha`/`review_head_sha` are None, call `changeset = await self._git.diff_summary(cwd, base_ref=state['review_base_sha'], head_ref=state['review_head_sha'])`, then `evaluation_prompt.build_prompt(criteria=..., changeset=changeset)`. In `_fix_code_node`, capture `pre_fix_head_sha = state['feature_tip_sha']` (raise if None); call `outcome = await self._merger.consolidate(base_branch=state['feature_branch'], feature_branch=state['feature_branch'], source_branch=fix_branch, ...)`; emit `WorkflowConsolidationEvent` (no phase field); on DIVERGENT/SOURCE_MISSING return state with `merge_error` populated, `feature_tip_sha=pre_fix_head_sha`, `merged=False`, `review_base_sha=None`, `review_head_sha=None`, `fix_rounds_used+1`; on FAST_FORWARDED/ALREADY_INTEGRATED return state with `feature_tip_sha=outcome.feature_tip_sha`, `review_base_sha=pre_fix_head_sha`, `review_head_sha=outcome.feature_tip_sha`, `fix_rounds_used+1`. Replace the unconditional `add_edge('fix_code', 'review_against_ticket')` with a conditional `add_conditional_edges('fix_code', self._route_after_fix, {...})` whose router is `def _route_after_fix(self, state): return 'review_against_ticket' if state['merge_error'] is None else ('comment_failure' if state['pr_url'] is not None and self._pr_creator is not None else 'complete')`. In `_complete_node`, source `final_commit_sha=state['feature_tip_sha']`. NO `try/except` anywhere around merger calls.
requiredChanges.rationale: Replaces the silent-skip + exception-bubble routing with a typed four-way switch on `ConsolidationOutcome.status`. The fix node uses `feature_branch` as `base_branch` for `consolidate` because the worktree must be acquired atop the current feature tip — the prior bug acquired atop `ctx.base_branch` (closing #5 Mode 3). Plumbing pre-fix tip into `review_base_sha` (40-char SHA) and post-consolidation tip into `review_head_sha` closes #12 deterministically for fix rounds. ALREADY_INTEGRATED on fix is legal — review re-runs against empty changeset and the empty-changeset escape clause fires (reviewer concern O: explicit mapping). DIVERGENT routing splits on `pr_url` between `comment_failure` and `complete` (reviewer concern P). NO phase field on the event (reviewer concern A).

Implement the three new async methods (`is_ancestor`, `remote_branch_sha`, `diff_summary`) recording `.calls`. Defaults preserve existing test behavior. Full rewrite of `FakeBranchMerger`: REMOVE the `fail` ctor param; REMOVE `merge_and_push`; REMOVE the public `cleanup_source` method; ADD `consolidate(*, ...) -> ConsolidationOutcome` that pops from a configurable `consolidation_outcomes: list[ConsolidationOutcome]` queue (default: one FAST_FORWARDED outcome with deterministic SHA); KEEP `cleanup_backup_branches`. Calls are recorded with `method='consolidate'` or `method='cleanup_backup_branches'`. Extend `FakeChangePersister` to include a `PersistSource` in its configurable result (default `WORKING_TREE_COMMIT`).

All ctor params keyword-only with defaults so existing tests are not broken.

Front-end consumer-schema migrations. The new `workflow_consolidation` SSE event type is added on the producer side; downstream consumer schemas (if any parse against a closed union) MUST update their schema. The snapshot test in `test_ralph_workflow.py` is the coordination artifact; explicit consumer-side migration is tracked separately.
openQuestions: Should the new `_log_release_state` warning trigger a structured SSE event in addition to the structured log, so the workflow-layer caller can observe dirty release? Recommendation: no — the warning log is sufficient for the bug-class fix; an SSE event would require a `WorkspaceReleaseAnomaly` event type and `WorkspaceProvider` access to the LangGraph stream writer (which it currently does not have). File separately if observability needs grow.

If `_review_against_ticket_node` is reached with `review_base_sha == review_head_sha` (ALREADY_INTEGRATED fix path), the digest is empty and the prompt's escape clause fires. The reviewer always returns `passed=False` in that case (no changes to evaluate) — which advances `fix_rounds_used` again. With `max_fix_rounds=2` the loop terminates correctly at `comment_failure` or `complete`. Is this the desired UX, or should `_route_after_fix` detect the empty-changeset case and route directly to `comment_failure` to skip the empty-review round? Recommendation: keep the current path — the empty review is a deliberate truth-telling step and lets the operator see in the SSE stream that the fix was a no-op.

The `_run_with_exit_codes` helper duplicates much of `_run`'s subprocess scaffolding. Should it be factored as a `_run_core(...) -> (exit, stdout, stderr)` with `_run` and `_run_output` as thin wrappers? Recommendation: yes — DRY win, but mechanical; can be done in the same change without expanding scope.
